summary: SendTimeGuard's destructor now logs via spdlog::error on discard()'s own throw (the SAFE-4 fix), but this new logging call is not exception-safe against a second failure, and the destructor is implicitly noexcept, so a second failure calls std::terminate(). Mechanism verified two ways: (1) read spdlog's actual shipped headers (logger.h): SPDLOG_LOGGER_CATCH catches std::exception and swallows it, but its catch(...) branch explicitly rethrows, and the fmt_lib::format call used to build the message is itself unguarded and can throw (bad_alloc, fmt::format_error) before the error handler ever runs -- spdlog::error is not provably non-throwing. (2) empirically confirmed the consequence with an isolated compiled repro: a destructor whose catch handler itself throws a second exception calls std::terminate (SIGABRT) on ordinary destruction, since destructors default to noexcept in C++11+. GCC will not flag the real code with -Wterminate since spdlog::error is an opaque call, not a literal throw -- exactly the class of defect only a lifetime review catches. TRIGGER: discard(command_id) throws inside the guards destructor AND the paired spdlog::error call in that same catch block also throws (fmt/allocation failure inside spdlog's own exception-formatting path, or a non-std::exception-derived throw that spdlog rethrows). Consequence: process-wide std::terminate, not merely the one request.
